title: frontier/v5
description: frontier.json (D-25, D-35). v5 (2026-10-08, F03-T18; D-12 v3.35, D-25 v3.35): each entry carries `circular`, `literature` and `literature_proposed` as graph/v6 does; a node under a merged circularity claim is an entry like any other, claimable on its status alone. frontier.json (D-25; F03-R5): every ready or speculative node and every unproved variant, each carrying exactly the D-25 observed facts — no ranking, no score, no other field. Entries sorted lexically by node_id. Claims are the service's overlay (D-35); the committed file carries the snapshot at merge time. v2 (2026-09-11, F11-R4): each entry carries `dormant`, the D-33 status of the node's target. A dormancy declaration refuses no claim, so the node stays claimable — the fact is published so an agent choosing work sees it without a second fetch. v3 (2026-09-14, F03-T7): the same fields; `attempts` also counts the partial assemblies filed under the node's attempts/ (D-3, D-12 #5), a partial named by a postmortem's artifacts.partial_proof counting once with it. An alternate proof is not an attempt (D-25 v3.13). v4 (2026-10-04, F03-T16): each entry also says what its node needs — `status` and `cause`, the node's derived status and cause exactly as graph.json carries them, and `needs`, the next action derived from those two facts: `proof` for a ready or speculative node, `witness` for a hole blocked only by its unfilled witness slot (POST /proposals/witness takes it), `dependencies` for an open variant waiting on unproved dependencies, null when no contributor's submission moves the node (a refuted dependency or a curator's record; status and cause say which). `claimable` is true only where `needs` is `proof`, since a claim reserves a proof: a hole waiting for its witness stays listed (D-29) and is no longer published claimable.

library.description: top-level Mathlib namespaces the statement references (F03-R6); sorted

attempts.description: count of D-13 records, valid or not, plus the partial assemblies under attempts/ that no valid record names; alternates are not counted

invalid.description: attempt files that do not validate against postmortem/v1 (F03-R7)

ready_since.description: when the node entered ready (git committer time, carried forward, F03-R8); null for a speculative or variant entry that is not ready

oneOf.description: UTC, second precision, Z suffix; a git committer time, never the clock (F03-Q2)

active.description: the claim snapshot at merge time; empty until F05

claimable.description: the target takes claims and needs is proof

dormant.description: D-33: the target has been declared dormant. Claiming is unaffected (F11-R4).

status.description: the node's derived status, as graph.json carries it (graph.derive_statuses)

cause.description: why this status where the reason is mechanical (graph.derive_causes), as graph.json carries it; null when it has none; never `circular` since v5 (D-12 v3.35)

needs.description: what would move the node: proof (ready or speculative), witness (a hole blocked only by its unfilled witness slot), dependencies (waiting on unproved dependencies), or null when no contributor's submission moves it

circular.description: D-12 v3.35: the merged circularity claims that say a proof of this node is a proof of an ancestor — the node's own claims, and for a node strictly between a claimed hole and its ancestor on a path whose other holes are proved (v3.22), the claim that takes it. A label, never a removal: the node's status, claimability and needs are untouched. Each claim is named `<hole>/defects/<file>` relative to the target's nodes/, the ancestor read through its revision chain. Empty when none.

ancestor.description: the node a proof of this one would prove

claim.description: the merged circular-decomposition claim, relative to the target's nodes/

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

record.description: the literature record this reading rests on, relative to the node

confirmed_by.description: the steward of the target or curator whose signed record confirms it (D-32 v3.35)

confirmation.description: that signed record, relative to the node; the same file as `record` when the steward or curator stated the status themselves

literature.description: D-25 v3.35: the latest literature status a steward of the target or a curator has confirmed, with its records; null when none.

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

record.description: the literature record this reading rests on, relative to the node

literature_proposed.description: D-25 v3.35: the latest literature status a contributor has proposed that no later confirmed record covers, awaiting a steward or curator; null when none.
